hyps.why: A direct skip into the output already provides a trainable path, so extra conv capacity on the two-hop edge is redundant.
Output-side conv capacity saturates once the direct edge is already a 3x3 conv.
Replacing none adds connectivity and capacity, whereas replacing an existing op only swaps transforms.
Replacing the identity on the direct path with a transform loses the clean gradient path.
Two pools in series on the 1->2->3 path over-smooth features.
Receptive field is already large after an upstream 3x3, so the series gain is small, especially at low resolution.
Skip helps by adding connectivity, but when it replaces a conv it removes capacity.
Upgrading a kernel size is a marginal change compared with adding a conv where there was none.
An identity into node 2 gives the downstream conv an un-smoothed input to build on, so the two are complementary.
Pooling after a conv follows the classic conv-pool pattern and is complementary rather than redundant.
